said on Wednesday that its banking subsidiary, DBS Bank, faced a lawsuit from liquidators of four companies seeking estimated damages of S$1.298B ($1.03B) linked to the 1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal (1MDB).
The lawsuit was filed by Affinity Equity International Partners, BlackRock Commodities (Global), Platinum Global Luxury Services, and TKIL Global Investments, along with their liquidators.
DBS Group categorically rejected the claim and said it will vigorously resist the lawsuit.
The bank noted that global recovery efforts related to 1MDB have been ongoing since 2018, but there had been no claim against the company during that period.

Moreover, the company added it has assessed the matter and does not require any provision at this stage, meaning the bank does not currently expect to recognize a financial provision related to the claim.
On the market side, the stock traded 1.63% lower at ~$243.56.

title: DBS Group faces $1.03B damage claim tied to 1MDB scandal
